title: Teach the canonical round through a short interactive How to Play flow
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md and the exact referenced imported design sections before editing. RULES-SPEC-v1.md is canonical for production mechanics: six-node Repair/Sabotage tracks, one-person crew votes, Route/Gate operations, deterministic powers and silent spectators. SCREEN-FLOW prototype 5/5 scores and hardcoded transitions are UX references only. Preserve historical T01–T10 APIs/tests; implement the new view version in new game-v1 modules instead of silently changing legacy five-mark boards or command parsers. Use black/charcoal/neutral-frost chrome and full-colour approved expressive content through semantic asset keys. Modal-first means the complete game background is uniformly blur/dim/desaturated and inert; the fixed platform banner dock remains mounted outside that game viewport. No visible accounts/login, telemetry, credentials, live Firebase, ad SDK or unreviewed asset downloads. Keep local presentation distinct from authority: clients display server/solo-engine phases and deadlines, never compute secret outcomes, choose timeout targets, advance multiplayer on a local clock or reveal another alignment. Use injected semantic media/ad/purchase ports; no direct SDK playback or billing calls from UI. Edit only ownership, use original fixtures, run scoped tests/lint/typecheck and npm run check. DOM tests use jsdom, explicit afterEach(cleanup), Vitest and current Testing Library. Report results and contract changes; do not commit, push, open PRs, deploy or spend on providers. Implement the shared-nav tutorial and local in-match help popup using canonical Rulesv1. Teach rotating Shift Lead, one-person direct card vote, top-two Crew with cooldown/Jam, complementary Route/Gate diagnostics, deterministic Repair/Sabotage/Anomaly and six-node wins. Use original explicitly synthetic examples that do not show another real player role or seed. No long wall of rules, old two-nominee Link approval, Repair/Sabotage buttons, five-mark win or Witness minigame. Allow step/back/close and keyboard use without dispatching actual gameplay intents.
acceptance: A short ordered interaction teaches every listed canonical action and makes Repair good/Sabotage bad clear.
Examples demonstrate ambiguity: a public result never proves the partner alignment or exposes the partner private option.
Tutorial navigation/help overlay is accessible, modal-first in a match and never pauses the online table.
No real intent, timer resolution, secret data access or local win evaluation occurs from tutorial interactions.
